A feature release. The theme is other agents — Codex sessions now get orbs
alongside Claude Code's, and an OpenClaw gateway's agents can too, with a chat
panel that works the same way for all three and can even talk back into a
local terminal. Still a beta, and this one leans on that word more than most:
most of what's below is macOS-only or has real, specific gaps — see *Known
limitations* before you rely on any of it.

## New: Codex CLI sessions as orbs

Codex sessions now show up as orbs — all three states, click-to-focus the
terminal — named the way Codex names them: `/rename` if you've set one, else
Codex's own auto-title from your first message, the same precedence Claude
Code already used. There's no `/color` equivalent in Codex, so a Codex orb
keeps a plain ring and a small badge instead of a colored one.

**A Codex orb only appears after you send your first message**, not when
Codex opens or a session is resumed. That's Codex's own behavior — it fires no
hooks until a thread actually exists — not something Buddy is choosing to
delay.

**Codex will not run a hook it hasn't been told to trust.** A `hooks.json` it
didn't write itself starts out untrusted, and the installer's own edits will
trigger that review the first time Codex starts afterward. Accept it (or run
`/hooks` and trust the entries by hand), or no hook ever fires, no orb ever
appears, and nothing anywhere tells you why.

Turn replying on under Settings → **Codex sessions**, the same shape as Claude
Code's own toggle, to get a compose line that types into the session's real
tmux pane — including answering Codex's numbered approval prompts from the
panel instead of switching to the terminal.

Fixing this also fixed a bug that could hit **Claude Code sessions**, not just
Codex ones: Claude Code running `codex exec` as a tool call spawns a Codex
process sharing its own pid, and the app used to track "which status file is
newest for this pid" without asking which CLI wrote it — so a Codex status
file could silently supersede and delete the Claude Code orb doing the actual
work. Confirmed and fixed by grouping on the pid *and* which CLI wrote the
file, not the pid alone.

## New: OpenClaw agents as orbs, and a chat panel that talks to them

Settings → **OpenClaw agents** connects to an OpenClaw gateway — off by
default, and nothing about it (no socket, no key, no gateway traffic) happens
until you turn it on. You'll need the gateway's **address** (an IP, not a
hostname — its certificate has no hostname to validate) and a **gateway
token**, kept outside `settings.json`. The first connection pairs this
install as a new device; approve it on the gateway side with
`openclaw devices approve --latest` and check that it's asking to approve
something named `gateway-client`.

Each active agent session gets its own orb, named **Agent — #channel**,
breathing the same way a local session's orb does. Click one to open the same
chat panel Claude Code and Codex sessions use — history, the agent's own
thinking, tool calls, a compose line, Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a
newline, and mic dictation if you have that on.

**Allow replying to agents** is a second, separate switch: writing needs a
second gateway pairing with write scope, so turning it on asks you to approve
that pairing too. **Show sessions active within** and **Keep orbs for**
control how far back into a gateway's history — which can be dozens of
sessions across days — this actually reaches for.

## New: one room, every agent in it, together

If more than one agent shares a channel, they now share **one orb** for it
instead of each getting their own. Opening it merges every agent's transcript
into a single conversation, each agent shown in its own color, with their own
echoes of each other's messages recognized and collapsed rather than shown
twice.

Sessions are also now badged by what kind they are: **⏱** for a scheduled or
cron job, **@** for a direct message, **#** for a channel, and no badge at all
for an agent's own main session (every agent has one, so a badge there
wouldn't distinguish anything).

## New: talk back to a local Claude Code session from the chat panel

The same chat panel gained a keyboard button for **local** Claude Code
sessions too — it tails the real transcript file and, when replying is turned
on, types your message into that session's actual tmux pane via `send-keys`,
the same mechanism click-to-focus already used. One reader, one writer — not
a synced copy of anything. Permission prompts are answerable from the panel
too, parsed off the real terminal rather than guessed. A session running
outside tmux stays read-only, since there's no pane to type into.

Markdown renders properly in the panel now instead of showing literal
asterisks and backticks — this was quietly wrong for gateway replies before
today's release too.

## Fixed: a flyout could open on the way to a different orb

Hovering an orb opened its flyout instantly, so a cursor traveling across a
dense stack toward a *different* orb would pop the first one's menu open in
the way. A 450ms hover delay fixes it; moving back to an orb from its own
already-open flyout skips the wait, since that's not a new request to open
one.

## Fixed: the high-quality voice engine could vanish across an upgrade

The engine installs to a version-specific folder, and the check for "is it
installed" compared against the *exact current version's* path — so updating
Claude Buddy at all could make a perfectly good, already-downloaded engine
report as missing, and every voice you'd picked would silently disappear from
the list. It now falls back to an older-but-present engine rather than
demanding an exact match, quietly re-fetches the current version's engine in
the background if you already had the feature turned on, and cleans up
superseded version folders that used to just accumulate (previously about
188MB per release, kept forever).

## Fixed, smaller

- Two sessions open in the same directory no longer fight over one saved orb
  position.
- A session key nested inside another session key no longer splits one room
  into two — observed for real: one channel became two rooms, the second
  misnamed by its raw internal id.
- A gateway orb's dragged position is now actually saved.
- Reply colors are consistent everywhere a reply shows up, not just inside a
  room's merged view.

## Which file do I want

| Platform | Download |
| --- | --- |
| macOS, Apple silicon (M1 and later) | `ClaudeBuddy-0.4.0-beta-osx-arm64.dmg` |
| macOS, Intel | `ClaudeBuddy-0.4.0-beta-osx-x64.dmg` |
| Windows 10/11, 64-bit | `ClaudeBuddy-0.4.0-beta-win-x64-setup.exe` |

The `ClaudeBuddySpeech-0.4.0-beta-*.zip` assets are the optional high-quality
voice engine. **You do not download these yourself** — the app fetches the
right one when you turn the setting on. They're published here because that's
where it looks.

The .NET runtime is bundled; nothing else is needed. `SHA256SUMS.txt` covers
every file — verify with `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt` on macOS or
`Get-FileHash <file> -Algorithm SHA256` on Windows.

## Upgrading from 0.3.0-beta

**macOS**: replace the app in Applications. The signing identity is
unchanged, so Automation permission and click-to-focus carry over. If you
already had the high-quality voice engine enabled, it re-fetches the current
version automatically — see the voice-engine fix above, this is exactly the
upgrade path that used to lose it.

**Windows**: run the new setup over the old one; it upgrades in place and
leaves your hook configuration alone.

Codex support and OpenClaw agents are both **off by default** and reach out
to nothing until you turn them on. If you want Codex orbs, you'll still need
to accept Codex's own hook-trust prompt the first time it starts after
whichever installer step wires the hook in — see *New: Codex CLI sessions as
orbs* above.

## Installing fresh

**macOS** — open the DMG, drag Claude Buddy to Applications, then
double-click **Install Claude Code Hooks.command**. Launch from Applications;
nothing appears in the Dock and no window opens, which is correct — look in
the menu bar.

**Windows** — run the setup. Per-user, so no UAC prompt. Leave both
checkboxes ticked; tick **"Wire hooks for Claude Code running inside WSL"**
too if you use it.

### The hook step is not optional

Claude Buddy learns about your sessions from a hook Claude Code (and, for
Codex sessions, Codex) runs. Until it's wired in, the app starts and runs
correctly and shows **nothing at all**. The installers offer to wire it up;
let them. Existing settings are backed up first, and re-running repairs
rather than duplicating.

Hooks are read once at session start, so **restart any open sessions** after
installing or updating.

## Known limitations

Everything below is macOS-only unless stated otherwise — none of this
release's new features have run on Windows or Linux at all yet, beyond code
that compiles for them.

- **OpenClaw is unverified beyond one gateway.** A second or differently
  configured gateway has never been connected to; certificate rotation and
  re-trusting a gateway with a changed cert have never actually been
  exercised; the amber "needs you" state doesn't work yet for gateway
  sessions (it needs an approvals scope the app doesn't request); an
  elicitation dialog that isn't a plain numbered list falls back to a
  terminal button that has never been triggered for real.
- **Rooms**: only cron/scheduled-session traffic was watched streaming live;
  whether a Discord-originated message streams identically has not been
  checked. Replying to a scheduled session's room was tested directly against
  the gateway, though — that one path is confirmed, not assumed.
- **Codex**: whether a hook declared to run asynchronously actually delivers
  its payload is unconfirmed — the amber "waiting" state for Codex depends
  entirely on this working. The exact shape of Codex's approval modal, and
  which keys answer it, hasn't been fully mapped either. Speaking a Codex
  session's latest turn aloud can currently read out the wrong session's text
  in one specific case — a known, unfixed gap, not something this release
  claims to handle.
- **The local-session chat panel** (typing into a real tmux pane) has been
  hand-tested, not covered by an automated suite yet.
- **Windows installers are unsigned** — SmartScreen warns; choose **More
  info → Run anyway**. macOS builds are signed and notarized and open
  normally.
- A session killed with Ctrl+C at a permission prompt can leave its orb stuck
  on amber. Right-click → *Reset this session to idle* clears it.

`docs/codex-findings.md` and `docs/openclaw-findings.md` record what was
actually measured versus assumed, in more detail than fits here, if you want
the long version — including a list of Codex behaviors that are still
genuinely unknown (whether a compacted rollout file is rewritten in place,
what a shell-approval payload's `cwd` field actually looks like, and a few
others).
